claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: The study evaluated SGLT2 inhibitors across heart failure trials to estimate effects on heart-failure hospitalisation, mortality, health status, and clinically relevant subgroups across the ejection-fraction spectrum.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we estimated the effects of SGLT2 inhibitors on heart failure hospitalisations, mortality outcomes, and health status overall, and in 14 clinically relevant subgroups.

claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: The investigators prespecified a meta-analysis of DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved and then extended the analysis post hoc to DAPA-HF, EMPEROR-Reduced, and SOLOIST-WHF.

A PubMed/MEDLINE systematic search covered randomised placebo-controlled SGLT2-inhibitor cardiovascular or kidney outcome trials published from Jan 1, 2015 through July 1, 2022, and eligibility was limited to studies enrolling at least 1000 participants with heart failure.
The preregistered search was run on July 1, 2022 and identified no additional eligible trials beyond the five prespecified/targeted trials.
The primary endpoint was time to cardiovascular death or first hospitalisation for heart failure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary endpoint of the meta-analysis was a composite of time to cardiovascular death or first hospitalisation for heart failure.

claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: Secondary endpoints included cardiovascular death, first hospitalisation for heart failure, cardiovascular death or any worsening heart-failure event, and all-cause death.

The primary endpoint was examined across 14 subgroup families: LVEF, diabetes, age, sex, race, region, KCCQ-TSS, BMI, eGFR, NYHA class, recent heart-failure hospitalisation, NT-proBNP, baseline MRA use, and baseline ARNI use.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The effect of SGLT2 inhibitors on the primary endpoint was examined across 14 subgroups of interest

claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: Efficacy analyses used all randomised participants in intention-to-treat datasets, with fixed-effects inverse-variance meta-analysis and Cochran Q tests for between-trial and treatment-by-subgroup heterogeneity.

Time-to-first-event effects were represented as Cox-model hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals, and NNT was calculated using the Altman-Andersen method with a weighted mean of trial median follow-up.

KCCQ responder analyses defined clinically meaningful improvement as a 5-point or greater increase and deterioration as a 5-point or greater decrease from baseline to 8 months, analysed by logistic regression.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: clinically meaningful improvement (≥5 point increase) or deterioration (≥5 point decrease) in each of the KCCQ scores from baseline to 8 months, analysed by logistic regression.

claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: The DELIVER plus EMPEROR-Preserved protocol was prespecified in the DELIVER academic statistical analysis plan and preregistered as PROSPERO CRD42022327527 before DELIVER unmasking; adding the other three trials was post hoc and registered as CRD42022347574.
The five included trials were assessed as high quality with low risk of bias, and the meta-analysis calculations used STATA version 16.1.
The five trials included 21,947 participants: DAPA-HF 4,744; DELIVER 6,263; EMPEROR-Reduced 3,730; EMPEROR-Preserved 5,988; and SOLOIST-WHF 1,222.
DAPA-HF and DELIVER evaluated Dapagliflozin: 10 mg orally once daily.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All trials were placebo-controlled and examined oral doses of the investigational therapy

claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved evaluated Empagliflozin: 10 mg orally once daily.

claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: SOLOIST-WHF evaluated Sotagliflozin: 200 mg orally once daily, titrated to 400 mg once daily depending on side effects.

claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: For the primary composite, the harmonised two-trial meta-analysis used the EMPEROR-Preserved definition of cardiovascular death or first heart-failure hospitalisation because subgroup data were available under that definition; a sensitivity analysis used the DELIVER composite including urgent heart-failure visits.

For cardiovascular death, the harmonised primary analysis excluded unknown or undetermined deaths from the cardiovascular-death definition; a sensitivity analysis counted them as cardiovascular deaths.
Safety outcomes were not directly compared or meta-analysed because DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved differed in event definitions, ascertainment, and reporting windows.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Adverse events were not directly compared or meta-analysed because of differential data capture and exact definitions

By 8 months, SGLT2-inhibitor participants were reported to be 10–20% more likely to have clinically meaningful health-status improvement and 10–20% less likely to have clinically important deterioration than control participants.

Clinically meaningful KCCQ improvement was more frequent and deterioration less frequent with SGLT2 inhibitors across each of the three KCCQ summary scores at 8 months, without evidence of heterogeneity by trial.

claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: The authors concluded that SGLT2 inhibitors reduce mortality and worsening heart failure and improve symptoms and overall health status across the ejection-fraction spectrum, and should be considered foundational heart-failure therapy irrespective of LVEF or care setting.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SGLT2 inhibitors should be considered foundational therapy in all patients with heart failure, irrespective of LVEF or care setting.

claim_atom_crosswalk.claim: The DELIVER plus EMPEROR-Preserved meta-analysis was prespecified and preregistered, but the supportive five-trial meta-analysis was post hoc and had no assigned alpha, so the authors stated that it could not be considered hypothesis testing.
